subject: visual-sgr
text:
- **CLI equivalent (no conformance claim):** amber SGR only on the `DIALOG` word, dim SGR on stale rows and bold SGR only on NAME column values (the callsign; design cli), always beside the word. As built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline) `viola list`'s human mode on a terminal writes bold on every NAME value (wrapped and unwrapped), the attention (amber) token on the `DIALOG` word only of a wrapped row with a pending dialog (its kind word plain), and a wrapped `stale` row dim from its first byte to its last (NAME dim and bold, `DIALOG` amber and not dim); the BAY line, caption, empty-board line and separator carry no SGR, and each state is still carried by its printed word (`stale`, `DIALOG <kind>`, `expired`, `budget-paused`, `unverified-cli`, the STATUS words `idle` / `busy`, the unwrapped rack's `n/a` cells). The colour decision reads `NO_COLOR` (present, an empty value included), `TERM` (exactly `dumb`; `256color`) and `COLORTERM` (the founder's own word, chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline `inputs#I2`) and whether stdout is a terminal; it writes no SGR under `--json`, a passthrough role or any of those rungs, and picks a truecolor / 256 / 16 depth (on Windows after enabling VT processing on stdout, restored afterwards; a failed enable writes none). On a terminal too narrow, an unwrapped NAME is cut to the column less 3 characters plus `...`, never inside a `\xHH` escape (the width from `viola_pty::host_size()`); a wrapped NAME is never cut, and piped output and `--json` keep every name whole.
 Checked by the `board_row_style_*` / `board_row_width_*` units and `cross_list_rows_style_each_span_beside_its_word_on_a_terminal`, `cross_list_rows_print_no_sgr_under_no_color_dumb_piped_or_json` and `cross_list_rows_truncate_an_unwrapped_name_only_on_a_terminal_too_narrow_for_it`; dim only on stale rows is proven at the unit tier only, its outer-PTY witness a CARRY on "Linux and macOS parity". viola emits zero SGR of its own under non-TTY / `NO_COLOR` / `TERM=dumb` / `--json` / `viola run` / a passed `viola revive`, and the revive refusal pairs and `--list` rows carry no ESC byte. Under `viola run` on Windows the outer-PTY stream also carries the ConPTY host's own SGR, cursor and query bytes (not viola's: the inbox host's as measured at chunk 2026-09-25-pty-wrapper-on-windows research fact 4, the sideloaded `OpenConsole.exe`'s `ESC[1t ESC[c ESC[?1004h ESC[?9001h` as measured at chunk 2026-09-29-sideloaded-conpty), so the windows-2025 `viola run` check is that viola's literals are absent, on both backends. `unable` / `fail` are never coloured. Checked with assert_cmd + portable-pty on `[windows-2025, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]`.
